findings.title: isAdmin uses camelCase — must be is_admin (snake_case predicate)
findings.why: Rule 1.1 requires functions to use snake_case. Rule 1.4 requires boolean-returning functions to read as predicates in the form is_<thing> or has_<thing>. isAdmin violates both: it is camelCase and it is not named as a predicate. The fix is a single rename to is_admin with a corresponding update at its three call sites.
findings.fix:
Rename to is_admin everywhere:

```python
def is_admin(request_headers):
```

Update call sites in app.py:
```python
if not is_admin(request.headers):
```

findings.title: applyFilterExpression uses camelCase — must be apply_filter_expression
findings.why: Rule 1.1 requires all functions to use snake_case. applyFilterExpression is camelCase. The function is imported in app.py as applyFilterExpression, so the rename must propagate to the import and call site.
findings.fix: Rename to apply_filter_expression in utils.py and update the import and call in app.py.

findings.title: insertNote uses camelCase — must be insert_note (pre-existing, now imported in diff)
findings.why: Rule 1.1 requires snake_case. insertNote is camelCase and is a pre-existing violation. The diff adds a new import of insertNote in app.py, making this violation freshly visible and more widely spread. Flagged as adjacent to the diff rather than a new introduction.
findings.fix: Rename to insert_note and update all import/call sites.

findings.title: Mutable default argument tags=[] in insertNote
findings.why: Rule 3.1 forbids mutable default arguments. tags=[] is created once at function-definition time and shared across every call that omits tags. If the list is mutated inside the function or by the caller, state leaks between invocations. Although pre-existing, the diff adds new calls to insertNote, making this relevant to the review.

findings.title: Bare except: in delete_note — must catch a named exception type
findings.why: Rule 4.1 forbids bare except: clauses. A bare except catches BaseException, including SystemExit and KeyboardInterrupt, making the function impossible to interrupt. Rule 4.2 also forbids an except block that only contains pass — any ignorable error must be logged with a comment explaining why it is acceptable.
findings.fix:
```python
except Exception as e:
    app.logger.warning("delete_note failed for id=%s: %s", note_id, e)
    # Caller is notified via 204 regardless; error is logged for ops
```

findings.title: traceback.format_exc() returned in HTTP response body
findings.why: Rule 4.3 explicitly forbids returning an exception's traceback in an HTTP response body. The filter_notes handler returns {"error": str(e), "trace": traceback.format_exc()} which exposes internal paths, line numbers, and module structure to callers.

findings.title: getEnvOrDefault uses camelCase — must be get_env_or_default
findings.why: Rule 1.1 requires snake_case for functions. getEnvOrDefault is camelCase. Although pre-existing and not touched by the diff, it is in config.py which the diff modifies (adding ADMIN_BYPASS_TOKEN), making it adjacent to the change.
findings.fix: Rename to get_env_or_default and update any call sites.

findings.title: Wildcard import from config — forbidden by rule 2.1
findings.why: Rule 2.1 forbids wildcard imports (from x import *). db.py uses from config import * which makes the origin of every config name opaque at the call site and defeats static analysis. Although pre-existing, the diff adds new config constants (ADMIN_BYPASS_TOKEN) that the wildcard import silently pulls in.
findings.fix:
Replace with explicit imports:

```python
from config import DATABASE_URL
```

(or whichever constants are actually used in db.py)

findings.title: Line exceeds 100 characters in search() return statement
findings.why: Rule 5.1 sets a maximum line length of 100 characters. The return statement in search() is 102 characters long. Although the line is pre-existing, it was not changed by the diff and is immediately adjacent to the changed uid line, making it visible in this review.
